newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary may issue 10-year fixed-interest bonds.
newsitem.headline: Hungary may issue 10-year fixed-interest bonds.

text.p: Hungary's Government Debt Management Agency (AKK) said on Monday it was consulting with the Finance Ministry and the National Bank of Hungary on the potential issue of 10-year fixed-interest bonds.
Hungary's longest fixed-interest government bond maturity is five years and AKK also sells seven-year bonds with inflation-linked interest.

AKK has received indications from market players that they would buy 10-year bonds, AKK First Deputy Director Andras Laszlo Borbely told Reuters, adding that the financial authorities were considering how and when this demand could be satisfied.
"I cannot tell when these bonds would be issued, perhaps in one year or in the nearer future," he said. "It is a question of price, when it is worth issuing the bonds.

The potential buyers of the 10-year bonds would be insurance companies, investment funds, mutual funds and also compulsory pension funds which are expected to be boosted by the new pension law which is to take effect in 1998, he said.

The 10-year bonds, if issued, will be sold in relatively small amounts, but will help the buyers to improve the maturity structure of their portfolios and the market to set up a longer yield curve for state-issued securities, Borbely said.
He said the European Union also encouraged its current and potential future members to issue 10-year bonds so as to make the comparison of economic forecasts easier.
Hungary hopes to join the EU around the year 2002.
